These terms are the agreement between you and **atpotato, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company, for your use of Virga. In them, “we”, “us” and “our” mean atpotato, LLC, and “Virga” means the website, its server and the software behind them.

Two parts of these terms change how a dispute with us would be handled: the limit on our liability, and the section on disputes, which sends most claims to individual arbitration and gives you 30 days to opt out of that. Please read both.

## What Virga is

Virga shows analytics for an account on the AT Protocol (atproto), the open network that Bluesky runs on, and gives you a place to write, schedule and look after that account’s posts.

- **Virga has no accounts of its own.** You sign in with an account that lives on a host you chose (your PDS). We don’t run that host, and we can’t create, recover or delete the account.
- **Virga is not Bluesky.** We are independent of Bluesky Social, PBC and are not affiliated with or endorsed by it.
- **Virga depends on services we don’t control.** These include your account’s host, Bluesky’s public API, the PLC directory and Constellation. If one of them changes, slows down or stops, parts of Virga will too.

## Who can use Virga

- You must be at least 13 years old, or the age at which you can consent to an online service where you live if that is higher.
- If you are under 18, or under the age of majority where you live, a parent or guardian must agree to these terms for you.
- You need an atproto account in good standing, and you must have the right to use every account you sign in with.

## Signing in and what Virga may do

You sign in on your account’s host, on that host’s own page. Virga never sees your password. The host gives Virga a limited permission that you approve there. It lets Virga:

- read your follower list and your notifications;
- follow and unfollow accounts, when you press the button for it;
- write, reply with and delete posts, and set who can reply to or quote them, when you ask it to;
- upload the pictures and video in your posts;
- read your saved posts and your reply settings, and search posts, for the composer;
- keep your drafts with Bluesky and your post templates in your own repository.

It does not let Virga like or repost, read your direct messages, change your handle, email or profile, or delete your account. Settings › Permissions lists every permission with the reason for it.

A sign-in is held one of two ways. A **browser session** stays in your browser. A **long session** is held by Virga’s server, which is what lets a scheduled post go out while your browser is closed. Signing out ends the session in that browser. You can also withdraw Virga’s permission at your account’s host at any time.

You are responsible for what is done through your accounts in Virga, and for keeping your devices and your host’s credentials secure. If you think someone else has used your account, sign out everywhere you can and tell your host.

Some of what Virga does changes your account, and some of it can’t be undone.

- **Posts.** A post you publish through Virga is public on the network, like a post made anywhere else. Deleting it afterwards asks your host to remove the record. It doesn’t recall copies that other services already hold.
- **Scheduled posts.** A scheduled or queued post is published by Virga’s server at the time you picked, whether or not you are there. Check what you schedule. We aim to publish within about a minute of the time, and we don’t promise that a post goes out on time or at all. A post set to repeat is published again at each time its rule names, until the rule ends or you stop it. A scheduled reply is not published if the post it answers is gone by then.
- **Post timers.** A timer acts when its time comes: it deletes the post, or changes who can reply to or quote it, unless a condition you set says to leave the post as it is. A deleted post is gone, and Virga can’t bring it back.
- **Follows and unfollows.** The tools that tidy up who you follow act on the accounts you select. Look at the selection before you confirm.

You decide what Virga does with your account, and you are responsible for the result.

You agree not to:

- break the law, or the rules of your account’s host or of any service you post to through Virga;
- use Virga to harass, threaten or stalk anyone. Reports such as who follows you, who has blocked you and which lists you are on are there to help you understand your own account, not to help you go after other people;
- send spam, or automate Virga beyond the scheduling and timers it offers;
- attempt to get around Virga’s limits, probe or attack its server, or reach data that isn’t yours;
- sign in to an account you don’t have the right to use;
- resell Virga, or present it as your own.

We may limit or suspend your use of Virga if you break these terms or put Virga, its users or other people at risk.

Virga works its numbers out in your browser, from your host, Bluesky’s public API and other public sources. They are the best count we can make from what those sources return, and they can be incomplete, late or wrong. Some reports say where they stop short, such as a very large follower list. Use them to inform your judgement; don’t rely on them for decisions with legal, financial or safety consequences.

## The post adviser and image descriptions

Virga has two optional features that use an AI model: an adviser that reads a post before it goes out, and image descriptions for alt text. The adviser is off until you turn it on. Either one sends what it needs to a model through Virga’s server, as the [Privacy Policy](PRIVACY_POLICY.md#the-post-adviser-and-image-descriptions) describes.

What a model writes can be wrong, incomplete or unsuitable. You decide whether to use it, and you are responsible for the post or the description that goes out under your name. These features have monthly allowances, which we may change.

## Your content

What you write and upload is yours. We claim no ownership of it.

To run the features you use, you give us permission to store, copy and send your content only as those features need: holding a scheduled post until it is published, passing your posts and uploads to your host, and sending a post or an image to an AI model when you ask for that. This permission ends when the content is no longer on our server, and it never lets us publish anything you didn’t ask us to publish.

You are responsible for your content, and for having the rights to post it.

## Other people’s information

Your archive contains public information about other people: the accounts that follow you, interact with you, block you or add you to lists. It is kept in your browser, or, in the iPhone and iPad app, on your device and in its backups, and you can export it. What you do with it is your responsibility, including under the privacy laws that apply to you.

Virga is free to use today. If we introduce paid features, we will say so before anything is charged, and nothing will be charged without your agreement.

Virga has limits, such as how many posts an account can have scheduled at once. We may change the limits, add or remove features, or stop offering Virga. If we stop, we will try to give notice first, and scheduled posts that haven’t gone out will not be published. Your account and everything in it stay with your host throughout.

If you send us ideas or feedback, we may use them without owing you anything.

Virga shows you posts from the network; it doesn’t publish them. A complaint about a post is best sent to the service that hosts it. If you believe something stored on Virga’s own server infringes your copyright, send a notice to the address under [Contact](#contact) with: your signature, physical or electronic; the work you say is infringed; what you say infringes it, and where it is; how to reach you; a statement that you believe in good faith the use isn’t authorised by the owner, its agent or the law; and a statement, under penalty of perjury, that the notice is accurate and that you are the owner or act for the owner.

Nothing in Virga is legal, financial, medical or other professional advice.

This includes losses from a post that was published, not published, or deleted; from an account you followed or unfollowed; from an action your host or Bluesky took against your account; and from reliance on a figure or on AI output.

# Privacy Policy

**Last updated:** November 23, 2026 (version 1)

This policy says what Virga does with information about you: what stays in your browser, what Virga’s server keeps, what is sent to other services, and what you can do about each. Virga is operated by **atpotato, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company, which is the controller of the information described here. “We”, “us” and “our” mean atpotato, LLC.

The short version:

- Your archive (your posts, followers, blocks and the rest of what the reports are built from) is worked out and kept in your browser, or on your device in the iPhone and iPad app. It is not sent to our server. The app’s copy is in your device’s backups unless you turn that off.
- Our server is involved only for what has to happen while your browser is closed, or that a browser can’t do alone: long sessions, scheduled posts, post timers, and the optional post adviser and image descriptions. It also keeps the record that your account agreed to our terms.
- Virga has no advertising, no analytics or tracking scripts and no cookies. We don’t sell information about you.
- You sign in on your own account’s host. Virga never sees your password and doesn’t collect your email address.

Two terms are used throughout. A sign-in is held either as a **browser session**, which stays in your browser and talks to your account’s host directly, or as a **long session**, which our server holds so that things can happen while your browser is closed.

## The network is public

Virga works with accounts on the AT Protocol (atproto), the open network that Bluesky runs on. Posts, follows, likes, blocks, lists and profiles there are public records that anyone can read. Most of what Virga shows you, about you and about the people around your account, is read from that public data. This policy covers what Virga does with it. It doesn’t cover your account’s host, Bluesky or other apps, which have policies of their own.

## What stays in your browser

Virga keeps the following in the browser you use it in. None of it is sent to our server unless this policy says so below.

| What | Where | How to remove it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your archive: your posts, followers, follows, blocks, the lists you are on, who interacts with you (their DIDs, handles, names and pictures), and every record in your repository | IndexedDB, one database per account | Settings › Data and sync deletes it. So does Remove from this browser, if you tick the box to delete what the account keeps here |
| Pictures and video attached to drafts | IndexedDB, per account | Deleting the draft, or Remove from this browser with the box ticked. Settings › Data and sync leaves them |
| The accounts you have signed in with (DID, handle, name, picture, when each was last opened) and which one is open | localStorage | Remove from this browser |
| A long session’s token, which lets this browser act as your account through our server | localStorage | Signing out |
| A browser session’s tokens and keys | IndexedDB, kept by the sign-in library | Signing out |
| Your dashboards, posting settings (including the adviser’s goals, notes and style reading), an unsent post (for a day), a copy of your templates, this month’s adviser count, the tools’ Keep lists and the notes you put on your charts | localStorage, per account | Remove from this browser, with the box ticked |
| A note that the account agreed to our terms, and when | localStorage, per account | The same |
| Theme, accent, density, how numbers and dates are written and other display preferences, the commands you last used from the command palette, and a random identifier written into your Bluesky drafts so they can tell devices apart | localStorage, per browser | Clearing the site’s data in your browser |
| A sign-in in progress, and a compose link opened before signing in | sessionStorage | Closing the tab |

A script running on the page could read what is kept here. That is true of every web app that keeps a session in the browser, and it is the reason to use Virga on a device you trust.

**The iPhone and iPad app** keeps the same things on your device. The archive and drafts’ pictures and video are files in the app’s own folder, sign-in tokens are in the device’s Keychain, and the rest is in the app’s settings. Your device’s backups, to iCloud or to a computer, include the app’s folder and its settings. To leave the folder out, turn off iCloud Backup in Settings › Data and sync; the settings are still backed up. Backups already made keep their copy until newer ones replace them. A backup is held by Apple under your Apple Account, or on your computer, and nothing in it reaches our server. Sign-in tokens are kept for that one device and are never in a backup, so after a restore you sign in again.

## What Virga’s server keeps

Our server is a set of functions hosted by Vercel, with a database and file storage at Supabase. It holds the following, and only for accounts that use the feature in the first column.

| Feature | What is kept | For how long |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Long sessions | Your account’s DID, the tokens your host issued to Virga and the key they are bound to, encrypted before they are stored. A fingerprint (SHA-256) of each browser’s session token, with the DID and an expiry date. The token itself is not stored | The tokens: deleted when our server receives a sign-out from the last browser holding the session. If that sign-out never reaches the server, or you withdraw Virga’s permission at your host without signing out, they stay (no longer usable, in the second case) and are not removed automatically today; you can ask us to delete them. A browser’s fingerprint: deleted when that browser signs out; otherwise it stops working within 30 days of its last use, and the expired row is not removed automatically today |
